content.intro: {state} charges a {stateRate} highway use tax instead of sales tax when you title a vehicle, plus a title fee and a yearly plate fee. Electric vehicles pay an extra yearly fee.

howItWorks.text: The highway use tax is {stateRate} of the price. At a dealer the price includes any administrative or document fee, and a trade-in comes off before the tax is figured.
If you bring a vehicle in from another state, the tax is capped, and you may get credit for tax you already paid elsewhere in the last few months if you can show proof.
The title fee is charged once. The plate fee is yearly, and the state raises DMV fees every four years based on inflation.
Electric vehicles pay an extra yearly fee and hybrids pay a smaller one. The county also bills property tax on the vehicle with the plate, and a few counties add transit taxes.

faq.q: Is there sales tax on a car in North Carolina?
faq.text: There is no sales tax. A highway use tax is charged when the vehicle is titled.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the tax?
faq.text: Yes. On a dealer sale the trade-in comes off the price before the tax is figured.
Only for vehicles brought in from another state. The tax on those is capped at a set amount.

faq.q: What else is billed with the plate?
faq.text: Your county bills property tax on the vehicle, and some counties add a transit tax and county vehicle tax. This calculator leaves those out.
Yes. They pay an extra yearly fee, and hybrids pay a smaller one.
